Before irreversible deduplication, compare the deletion candidate and a retained counterpart across all user-visible identity-bearing content, including ingredients, directions, quantities/servings, duration and other relevant metadata; missing fields remain unknown, not equal.

Keep batching: gather bounded JSON-compatible candidate snapshots in observation batches, then execute guarded known navigation/delete/confirm chains only for already-proven pairs. Re-read candidate identity immediately before confirmation and stop on mismatch.
Keep one verified survivor per exact-equivalence group and an explicit deletion ledger; do not stop at one item per description bucket.
Do not zip separately sampled title/description lists or interpret viewport element counts as database cardinality. Use card-scoped paired facts and bounded coverage tracking.
On apparent count stasis, reconcile with read-only stable observations before more deletions; additional matching cards are not evidence that the prior deletion failed.

Reserve actions for comparison and preservation, not merely deletion throughput. If evidence cannot establish equivalence within remaining actions, preserve uncertain records and report an unverified outcome rather than asserting completion.
Report only what the final observation proves; local success and session cleanup are distinct from collection-wide correctness.
